question: Shared, once the right document is read: prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, with MRI as the shared channel. P-211 (Cai et al., Brain Sci 2023) uses an Explainable Boosting Machine on baseline FreeSurfer regional volumes/thickness plus cognitive scores, demographics and APOE4, at horizons of 1-5 years. The ledger's P-174 figure (AUC 0.827) is Bae et al. 2021 (P-37 in the corpus): a transfer-learned 3D CNN on a single baseline T1 image for conversion within 3 years against MCI stable for at least 3 years. The PDF mapped to P-174 is a different paper (Xu et al., MEG graph embedding, Madrid cohort) that prints no 0.827. P-174 is a dedup stub of Bae et al. and must not be cited. Horizon and feature set differ, which condition 1 allows.

figures.P-211: Five-year horizon, Comb (a) (MRI + cognitive + demographics + APOE4): AUC 0.92, accuracy 85%; 225 participants remain at 5 years (140 MCI/85 dementia). The figure is a mean with SD error bars in Figure 2, no interval printed. Hanley-McNeil over the 5-fold CV sample (n1 = 85, n2 = 140): Q1 = 0.92/1.08 = 0.8519, Q2 = 2(0.92^2)/1.92 = 0.8817, SE = 0.0214, CI [0.878, 0.962]. Over a 10% test set (about 9/14): SE 0.0676, CI [0.788, 1.000]. Three-year horizon, test data: AUC 0.81 with interaction effects (0.78 without); 3-year cohort 580 (392 MCI/188 dementia). Over a 10% test set (about 19 dementia/39 MCI): Q1 = 0.6807, Q2 = 0.7250, SE = 0.0659, CI [0.681, 0.939]; over the whole 3-year cohort (188/392): SE 0.0207, CI [0.769, 0.851]. The 0.78 figure: CI [0.644, 0.916] at the test-set n.
figures.P-37 (the ledger's P-174 claim): AUC 0.827, accuracy 82.4% on a single held-out test set of 68 scans. The test set holds 37 MCI-C (conversion 0-3 years; sensitivity 81.08% = 30/37) and 31 MCI-NC (56/68 correct overall). No AUC interval printed. Hanley-McNeil with n1 = 37, n2 = 31: Q1 = 0.827/1.173 = 0.7050, Q2 = 2(0.827^2)/1.827 = 0.7487, SE = 0.0498, CI [0.729, 0.925].

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists and reconciles the pair. P-211 reports its result at P-37's three-year horizon: AUC 0.81 with interaction effects (0.78 without). 0.81 and 0.78 both lie inside P-37's interval [0.729, 0.925]. P-37's 0.827 lies inside P-211's three-year interval under either evaluation-set assumption ([0.681, 0.939] at the test-set n; [0.769, 0.851] at the whole 3-year cohort). The matched figures agree in both directions. The headline gap is a horizon effect: 0.92 is P-211's five-year figure, and P-211 describes its AUC falling to a low point at three years. Even the headline pair is only marginally apart. 0.92 lies inside P-37's interval (upper bound 0.925), and 0.827 lies outside P-211's five-year interval only if the 0.92 is taken over the 225-participant CV sample.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: 0.92 and 0.827 are below 0.97.
reason: Read against the right document (Bae et al., P-37), the pair shares the question, the MRI channel and the metric. The ledger's headline gap (0.92 vs 0.827) sets P-211's five-year AUC against a three-year result, and even that gap exceeds uncertainty in one direction only and under one evaluation-set assumption. At the matched three-year horizon P-211 prints AUC 0.81, which agrees with 0.827 in both directions, so the papers' own figures dissolve the gap and condition 3 fails. The operator named this pair; on the source documents it does not qualify. If it were ever reported, the ledger pair would need repointing from the P-174 stub to P-37.

quotes.quote: The five-years prediction accuracy reached 85% (AUC = 0.92) using both cognitive scores and MRI markers.
The baseline information was used as input of all EBMs and the converting AD or not during follow-up period was used as output. All EBMs were tested with the 5-fold cross validation.
The dataset is divided into training and test sets with a percentage, respectively, of 90% and 10%.

The mean AUC using Comb (a) displayed a characteristic pattern of first at about 0.9, then decreasing, reaching a low point at 3 years, followed by a gradual increase until 5 years of follow-up, to about 0.92.

The main performance indicators, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects) compared to 0.72, 0.76, 0.68, and 0.78 (without interaction effects), respectively.

In the target task, we examined MCI-C patients with a conversion time of up to 3 years (longer conversion times are examined later) to MCI-NC patients with a clinical diagnosis that remains MCI for a duration of at least 3 years.
MCI-C and MCI-NC scans were randomly split into training, validation, and test sets by following the conventional ratio of 70% versus 15% versus 15% (314, 68, and 68 scans, respectively).
It produced a test set classification accuracy of 82.4% and 0.827 area under the curve as well as 0.189 equal error rate value
In conversion times from 0 to 3 years, 3 to 6 years, and 6 to 10 years, there were 37, 39, and 9 MCI-C subjects
MG2G achieved high performance with 61% for NC/sMCI/pMCI classification, 79% for NC/sMCI classification, 78% for sMCI/pMCI classification
